strings.en:
The fractals are completely realized now. It's just incredible to witness. I'm headed to the observatory later today with Dagda to run a few experiments but I've an...acute sense of dread. My blood refuses to still. I've never been to the observatory myself, so I've no reason to be anxious, but... I can't shake these feelings, although it's challenging to articulate them. Maybe I'm ill...? I haven't taken a day to myself in weeks.  

Apparently the observatory was one of the first "manufactured" or "conjured" fractals, so I'm curious to see inside at least. Isgarren and Waiting Sorrow used it to observe the other fractals as they formed, whether created or naturally occurring. Seer magic. Dagda is hopeful (or maybe desperate) that we can learn *something* inside, but that's starting to feel like false hope...  

Zojja made it sound completely nonfunctional, but Dagda's become progressively more...erratic over the past few days. Poring over Sorrow's notes, looking for things that aren't there. I know she misses her mentor, but I really need mine.

The jungle is brimming with those...creatures. Demonic, smelly, and revolting. Just...gross. They're ruining this forest. I've made a habit of killing them on sight to help preserve the jungle, but they return every morning.   
  
I was complaining about my quandary over our nightly supper fire when a traveler said the beasts took on an entirely new form when he encountered them in the Shiverpeaks a week or so ago—he also called them "titans," so at least I have a name to spit now. While these titans have taken on the jungle's mossy disguise, titans in the north are mimicking the icy mountain surroundings. Not only are they invasive, they are clearly very adaptive. I don't envy a lesser hunter trying to take one down, but I worry about what might happen if one crawled into a volcano...or a geyser.

strings.en:
Greetings, adventurer!

I'm Chief Melodist Flac, and I'm thrilled to introduce you to my wonderful new device. As you've traveled the world, surely your heart must have been captured by the work of local musicians. Maybe you've developed a taste for the work of underground bands in the Black Citadel, or even spent the night at one of those exclusive Lion's Arch dance clubs, eh? 

Has a tune ever gotten stuck in your head? Don't you wish you could listen to it again whenever you desire? 

Well, I've developed a device for precisely that purpose! I call it a jukebox, and it can read music recordings pressed into grooves—or "tracks," if you will—on easily stored disks. The only limit to how many songs you can store is the number of tracks you collect.
 
I've sent you the instructions for making your own jukebox, and I've even taken the liberty of sending you one completed device. You can find it in your home instance. Add one to your homestead today, and let the music move you!

Poor Project Selection:  
  
When our vessel crashed, I presumed we had all the evidence required to evaluate this coral worthy of a wide berth. Instead, after rescuing Arch Researcher Tunsi, I'm getting dragged along after his latest obsession. Meanwhile, the rest of our team seems to resent my calls for greater caution. Left to their own devices, I worry they'd tear me apart for sport and scholarship.  
   
Castora contains such a wondrous myriad of flora and fauna, each presenting prime opportunities for weaponization. The local crustaceans alone have such novel adaptations and potential for improvement! Laser crabs! To my intellect, it seems so obvious.  
  
But no. Tunsi insists upon weaponizing the volatile coral that surrounds the entirety of Castora. Already our tests reveal uncomfortable signs of low-grade sentience. Analysis of recent exposure subjects suggests this coral may well even have a capacity for violence. Perhaps even vengeance. If I was not so anxious, I might admire it. Still, I worry what ruin our research may leave in its wake.

Yesterday I found a batch of peculiar jade in mother's latest payload. It held a charge—a magic I've never seen before. She confirmed that she had never seen anything like it either. They'd just broken ground in a new location southwest of the Harvest Temple, and all the jade had come from there.

On a lark, I replaced the amber core in my lantern with a piece of the jade—the result nearly blinded me! The radiance was so intense! I made some adjustments and found that I had to reduce the flow of magic from the stone by a factor of approximately twelve for it to become bearable.

A factor of twelve! What could we achieve with that kind of power?

The situation in the Kaineng fractal has deteriorated rapidly. The jade mechs were designed to keep the city clean and productive, and once they achieved sentience they quickly optimized for that, determining that organic life was the primary impediment to that goal. When their initial command that organics leave the city was not obeyed, violence became their prompt solution. Their takeover of the city is already nearly complete, and the possibility remains that they will desire to expand their control.

Conclusion: This kind of machine intelligence being developed remains a significant concern for Tyria, and it raises the troubling possibility that similar constructs might already exist outside of Tyria. We recommend continuing to study scenarios like this until a better prevention plan is developed.

This list of financial records and personal files is indecipherable at first glance. However, upon closer inspection, it appears to be tracing the wealth and gatherings of suspected Purist sympathizers. A small memo is pinned to the top:

"I'm unsure if there's anybody left to read this, but if this message is ever found, don't expect to find anything more here. I've compiled a list of agents and enterprises my grandfather was convinced were tied to the old Purist regime, plotting against the empress from within. It was his last request that I do this. I'm honoring it, but I can't indulge these fantasies anymore.

I'll be reporting his suspicions to the Ministry of Security, and if there's anything of note in these conspiracies, they'll take it from there. If some sort of secret resistance against the Purists did at one time exist, it died out long ago."
